title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 94
paragraphs: Their belief in immortality is of this kind: they hold that they do not die, but that he who is killed goes to Salmoxis, a divinity (whom some of them call Gebeleizis). At intervals of four years they send one of their own people, chosen by lot, as a messenger to Salmoxis, charging him with such requests as they have to make on each occasion. They send him thus: certain men appointed for this hold three javelins, and others meanwhile take hold of the man being sent to Salmoxis, both by his hands and feet, and first they swing him up, then throw him into the air so that he falls upon the spear points. If he is pierced through and killed, they think the god is favourable to them; but if he is not killed, they find fault with the messenger himself, calling him a worthless man, and then, having faulted him, they send another. They give him the charge beforehand, while he is still alive. These same Thracians also shoot arrows up towards the sky when thunder and lightning come, and use threats against the god, believing that no other god exists except their own.
